description:
Team Believers is a passionate team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
Our project, Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, inspires young minds to explore space.
We aim to make astronaut training fun through interactive missions and educational activities.
We believe in innovation, teamwork, and inspiring the next generation of space explorers.
summary:
ASTRAVA is an interactive 3D space mission simulator designed to help students experience the challenges of becoming an astronaut rather than just learning about space through textbooks. We developed a browser-based game where players can create their own missions by choosing between the Moon and Mars, selecting a spacecraft, assigning crew members and their roles, and preparing for exploration.

Inside the spacecraft, players can explore different operational areas, manage essential resources, make mission-related decisions, and respond to unexpected challenges. The aim is to make space exploration more practical, engaging, and educational.

ASTRAVA addresses the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by turning real-world space exploration concepts into an interactive learning experience. It helps students understand teamwork, problem-solving, resource management, and the responsibilities astronauts face during missions. We believe learning about space should be more than reading about it; students should have the opportunity to experience the decisions and challenges that make every space mission possible.
details:
ASTRAVA – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

ASTRAVA is a 3D space exploration and mission-training experience that we developed to make learning about space more interactive and exciting. We wanted to create something where students would not just read about astronauts and their missions but actually experience some of the responsibilities and challenges involved in space exploration.

When players start a new mission, they first choose whether they want to explore the Moon or Mars. They can then customize their spacecraft, select their crew members, assign roles, and prepare their mission. Once everything is ready, they enter a 3D spacecraft where different rooms serve different purposes, just like the different systems and operational areas needed for a real space mission. The idea is to let players explore their spacecraft, understand how its systems work, and experience the decisions astronauts have to make during a mission.

Through ASTRAVA, we want to make complex space exploration concepts easier to understand, especially for students who are interested in science, technology, and engineering. It encourages curiosity, problem-solving, decision-making, and teamwork while giving learners a better understanding of what it takes to manage a space mission.

We developed the project using JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Vite, and Three.js. Three.js is used to create the interactive 3D environment, while Vite provides the development setup for running the project in a web browser.

The creative aspect of ASTRAVA is that players are not limited to watching a predefined space journey. They get to make their own mission choices, explore their spacecraft, and take responsibility for different aspects of the mission. We wanted to combine the experience of a space exploration game with the educational value of an astronaut training simulation.

During development, we considered scientific relevance, educational value, user experience, accessibility, and technical limitations. Our main focus was to make the experience engaging without losing its connection to real space exploration. Ultimately, we hope ASTRAVA can inspire more young people to explore space science and imagine themselves contributing to future missions to the Moon and Mars.
